threshold_mw.value: 75 MW: a new facility with a peak load forecast reasonably expected to reach a monthly maximum demand of 75 MW or more during the term, or an existing customer whose demand is reasonably expected to expand by 75 MW

cites.quote: reasonably expected to be equal to or in excess of a monthly maximum demand of seventy-five megawatts (75 MW) at any time during the Term
Any existing Customers, who as of the effective date of Schedule LLPS, have a monthly maximum demand that is reasonably expected to expand by seventy-five megawatts (75 MW).
The new LLPS rates will apply to any new facility beginning service with a peak load forecast at 75 megawatts (75 MW) or more, or an existing customer expecting to expand by 75 MW.

min_demand.value: Minimum Demand of 80 percent of the annual Contract Capacity, used for the Minimum Monthly Bill

cites.quote: Minimum Demand: Minimum Demand shall be 80% of the annual Contract Capacity.
Customers on the plan will pay a minimum monthly bill based on 80% of their contract demand, regardless of actual usage.

contract_term.value: Minimum term of up to five years of optional transitional load ramp plus twelve years; automatic five-year extensions unless either party gives at least 36 months' notice

cites.quote: Schedule LLPS Customers shall take service for a minimum term that includes up to five (5) years of an optional transitional load ramp period plus twelve (12) years.
the LLPS Service Agreement will automatically extend for periods of five years
The contract term will be a minimum of 12 years, plus an optional load ramp period of up to 5 years, which most customers are expected to use, for a total contract length of 17 years.

collateral.value: Two years of Minimum Monthly Bills, provided when the LLPS Service Agreement is executed (guarantee, letter of credit or cash); exemptions of 60, 50, 40 or 25 percent for customers meeting credit rating and liquidity tests, the 60 percent discount capped at $175 million (50 percent at $150 million, 40 percent at $125 million, 25 percent at $75 million)

cites.quote: The Company will require Schedule LLPS Customers to provide collateral in an amount equal to two (2) years of Minimum Monthly Bills, as calculated by the Company
will be exempt from sixty (60) percent of the Collateral Requirement, with the sixty (60) percent discount not to exceed $175 million.
will be exempt from fifty (50) percent of the Collateral Requirement, with the fifty (50) percent discount not to exceed $150 million.
will be exempt from forty (40) percent of the Collateral Requirement, with the forty (40) percent discount not to exceed $125 million.
will be exempt from twenty-five (25) percent of the Collateral Requirement, with the twenty-five (25) percent discount not to exceed $75 million.
The Collateral Requirement must be provided at the time of executing the LLPS Service Agreement.
They will also be required to provide collateral equal to two years of minimum monthly bills.

exit_fee.value: 36 months' written notice to terminate or change schedule; Exit Fee equal to the nominal value of the Minimum Monthly Bill times the months remaining in the Term or Extension Term, or 12 months, whichever is greater; with less notice, an Early Termination Fee of the Exit Fee plus two times the Minimum Monthly Bill times the months short of 36

cites.quote: the Customer must provide written notice thirty-six (36) months prior to the requested date of termination or schedule change.

the Customer will be subject to an Exit Fee equal to the nominal value of the Minimum Monthly Bill times the number of months remaining in the Term or Extension Term, or for twelve (12) months, whichever is greater
the Early Termination Fee shall be equal to the Exit Fee plus two (2) times the nominal value of the Minimum Monthly Bill times the number months less than the thirty-six (36)
If the contract is terminated early, an exit fee will apply that will require the customer to pay all minimum bills that would have been billed had the customer continued service.

rows.license_basis: The clause that answers the question (the sheets' issuing utility names Evergy Kansas South, Inc., and the rate area), the sheet terms and the current effective date were read only on evergy.com. Evergy's Terms and Conditions (https://www.evergy.com/terms-and-conditions, read 26 November 2026 after the sheet) bar any robot, bot, spider, scraper or other automatic device used to monitor or copy pages without Evergy's prior written permission, and allow a single copy for personal use. As with centerpointenergy.com in session 5300, the sheet was read before the terms, so the row is internal and evergy.com is not read further. This dataset's row ameren_evergy_spp-07 holds the same Kansas LLPS rule for Evergy Kansas Central and Evergy Kansas Metro with status approved (2025-11-06); this row adds that the sheets name Evergy Kansas South, Inc. among the issuing utilities, and that the sheets were reissued (27-EKCE-0151-TAR, approved 29 October 2026, effective 1 November 2026), a status change for that row to check against a public copy.
rows.notes: The question asked was whether the Kansas LLPS tariff applies to Kansas Gas and Electric Company's (Evergy Kansas South's) service area. As the sheets print it: the issuing utility is 'Evergy Kansas Central, Inc., & Evergy Kansas South, Inc., d.b.a. Evergy Kansas Central' and the territory is the 'Evergy Kansas Central Rate Area'; the sheets do not name Kansas Gas and Electric Company, and no document read states that Evergy Kansas South, Inc. is the former Kansas Gas and Electric Company (the brief's identification, not cited). The public KCC documents read (news release of 6 November 2025, slides of 15 January 2026) do not name Evergy Kansas South. Other sheet terms: capacity may be reduced after the first five years by the lower of 25 MW or 10 percent of Contract Capacity without charge (Sheet 4), larger reductions with 36 months' notice and a Capacity Reduction Fee (Sheet 5); collateral may be reduced at the Company's discretion after the customer has operated above 100 MW for five years (Sheet 10); a 25 percent credit on cash collateral up to $40 million in the first five years (Sheet 11). Rates on Sheet 3 (customer charge $386.67 a month, demand $22.985 summer and $20.817 winter per kW, energy $0.00872 per kWh, grid $0.248 substation and $0.156 transmission per kW) match those row ameren_evergy_spp-07 gives from the KCC report. Waits: a public copy of the reissued sheets (the KCC's docket system, kcc-connect.kcc.ks.gov, answered earlier readers with a bot check and was not tried) and a primary statement of the Evergy Kansas South and Kansas Gas and Electric identity (Evergy's FERC Form 1 for Evergy Kansas South sits on evergy.com, not read).
